conventions.convention: A group-like p-form symmetry has closed embedded supports of codimension p+1, total invertible fusion, and an effective action on complete admitted insertion and background data. Its label group is required to be Abelian for p>0; p=0 permits non-Abelian groups.
Crossing U_g⋆U_h means crossing U_h and then U_g, so ρ_gh=ρ_g∘ρ_h. Character charges are continuous homomorphisms to U(1), distinct from transformation labels.

Continuous U(1) p-form backgrounds are degree-(p+2) differential characters on smooth integral (p+1)-cycles, with boundary holonomy exp(i∫H) and curvature periods in 2πZ. Backgrounds are nondynamical, and their coupling is additional model input.

The Maxwell example uses real curvature after identifying ia with a, flux ∫S²F=2πm, and U_α(Σ)=exp(iα∫ΣF/(2π)). Normal orientation places the positive line tangent first; intersection signs use the ordered basis (line tangent, track basis).
The S3 example composes permutations by (στ)(j)=σ(τ(j)), uses permutation matrices on C³, zero Hamiltonian, and normalized mixed-insertion correlators Tr(O₁⋯Oₙ)/3.

load_bearing.statement: For d≥1 and 0≤p<d, a group-like p-form global symmetry consists of a locally compact Hausdorff group G, Abelian when p>0, and invertible topological defects of codimension p+1 with total group fusion, compatible crossing and background actions, complete-correlator covariance, and effectiveness. A continuous scalar homomorphism to U(1) is a character charge.

Let d≥2 and 1≤p<d. For the defined group-like symmetry, admissible pairwise local exchange isotopies identifying composite crossing and background maps imply G is Abelian. Separately, a unitary representation implementing crossing by conjugation on bounded operators makes the continuous scalar action on a nonzero bounded genuine simple p-dimensional operator a continuous U(1) character.

published_dependencies.used_for: The Maxwell example explicitly inherits AC_ω through its principal-connection and curvature suppliers; the definition states choice for every sequence of nonempty sets.

Finite smooth-chain Stokes establishes curvature-period integrality, source-free surface invariance, and the punctured-track linking formula. Integer chains are admissible special cases of the supplier's real chains.

concerns.concern: The flux and linking calculations establish topological surface functions and their phase relation, but the conclusion that these realize the preceding symmetry definition lacks part of that definition's interface. The Example requires only that 'Gauge changes transport configurations and b' with pullback covariance; it does not specify magnetic-symmetry bijections ρ_α on complete typed inputs, β_α on background/boundary data, or verify C(β_α(b);ρ_α(I))=C(b;I). Ordinary principal-bundle gauge covariance does not supply this magnetic symmetry action. In particular, T_m is a fixed sector label rather than an element of the function space, so step 3.2's 'pointwise relation' involving T_m also needs a declared linear extension or crossing rule on line insertion data. The arbitrary linear functional supplied here need not satisfy an additional symmetry-covariance law. The stronger realization claim therefore needs explicit model assumptions and verification; the conditional flux/phase calculation itself is sound.

seams_checked.note: The symmetry definition faithfully restates the supplier's closed embedded supports, complete model data, and decorated isotopy invariance avoiding other insertions and fixing boundary/background data.

The page declares this prerequisite, but its two items make no load-bearing citation to the principal-connection or curvature results. No stronger gauge-geometric proposition is attributed to the supplier.

The Maxwell example uses the supplied smooth right-principal connection convention, A_j−A_i=dθ_ij after real U(1) identification, trivial adjoint action, and Abelian Bianchi identity dF=0. AC_ω is retained, and smoothness is restricted to the complement of the magnetic line.

The realization definition preserves the ordinary finite Abelian one-form branch, genuine-line and complete-defect conventions, and permits a non-Abelian zero-form group with mixed Postnikov data. Its scalar-charge argument independently uses finiteness and a specified linear representation, without borrowing the charge theorem's conclusion while omitting its Hilbert-space hypotheses.

The anomaly and matching-data definitions use the zero-form symmetry/background interface and retain nondynamical backgrounds. They do not infer gauging, anomaly cancellation, or continuum existence from the symmetry definition.
